messages.subject: brainGraph_permute function error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,
I have a slight issue with the brainGraph_permute function which seems to be putting out a weird error, essentially saying it it is outputting a longer set of regions than intended? (The custom atlas has 308 regions).

myPerms <- permute::shuffleSet(n=nrow(all.dat.resids$resids.all), nset=kNumPerms)
perms.btwn <- brainGraph_permute(median.density, all.dat.resids, perms=myPerms, level='vertex')
Error in setnames(res.perm, 2:ncol(res.perm), regions) :
  'old' is length 309 but 'new' is length 308

I am running R version 3.5.0 (2018-04-23) and BrainGraph version 2.2.0.

Any help or advice would be greatly received!

BW
Danz

messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Problems when plotting clustering coefficient
messages.body_plain:
Are you referring to Chapter 12.2 of the User Guide? If so, you are correct and
have spotted an error. The variable should be called "small.tidy" as it was
created in an earlier code block. It is created as follows:

small.tidy <- melt(small.dt, id.vars=c('density', 'Group', 'N'))

Of course, this variable can be called whatever you prefer, as long as you are
consistent.

Regarding "mylabels.sm <http://mylabels.sm>",

mylabels.sm <http://mylabels.sm> <- small.dt.m[, levels(interaction(Group, variable))]
mylabels.sm <http://mylabels.sm> <- gsub('\\.Cp', ', Cp', mylabels.sm <http://mylabels.sm>)
mylabels.sm <http://mylabels.sm> <- gsub('Cp\\.', '', mylabels.sm <http://mylabels.sm>)

Note however that this is specific to plotting both the "simple"- and MC-based
approaches to generate random graphs, as shown in Figure 12.1

Let me know if this works,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Problems when plotting clustering coefficient
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've tried to used what you told me but R displays

Error: Insufficient values in manual scale. 20 needed but only 6 provided.

This, I understand, is because it uses every variable, not the ones I want to use ("Control, Cp", "Patient, Cp", "Control, rand", "Patient, rand", "Control, latt", "Patient, latt") to plot the graph. Finally what I've done is the following:

small.m <- data.frame(small.dt$density, small.dt$N, small.dt$Cp, small.dt$Cp.rand, small.dt$Cp.latt, small.dt$Group)
colnames(small.m) <- c("density", "N", "Cp", "rand", "latt", "Group")
small.dt.m <- melt(small.m, id.vars=c('density', 'Group', 'N'))
mylabels.sm <- c("Control, Cp", "Patient, Cp", "Control, rand", "Patient, rand", "Control, latt", "Patient, latt")

ggplot(small.dt.m, aes(x=density, y=value, col=interaction(Group, variable),
                       lty=interaction(Group, variable))) +
  geom_line(size=1.25) +
  scale_linetype_manual(name='Group, type',
                        labels=mylabels.sm,
                        values=rep(1:3, each=2)) +
  scale_color_manual(name='Group, type',
                     labels=mylabels.sm,
                     values=rep(c('red', 'cyan3'), 3)) +
  labs(x='Density', y='Clustering coefficient')

What this code does is select from the main data frame small.dt, the varibles of interest. Then, I assign the column names and create small.dt.m (with the same code you created small.tidy). I also set the labels (the code you gave me creates the labels for all the variables not the ones you display on the image of the manual).

This code works perfectly. Thanks for your help!

Hello again Chris,

I am writing because I now have a problem related to Adjacency matrix plots. The code you give is

                               g=g[[1]][[10]], group=groups[1])

                               g=g[[1]][[10]], group=groups[1])

print(matplot.lobe2)

Error: Insufficient values in manual scale. 23 needed but only 22 provided.

 - attr(*, ".internal.selfref")=<externalptr>

As you can see, I've highlighted in blue the rows of memb and color for both data.table. I don't know how to make it have the same number of memb and color. Also, I don't know if this error is due to having a brain segmentation too small and there are too many comunities.

Regards,
